notes: Only the advertised tools `execute_sql` and `search_objects` were judged. `explain_sql`, `health_check`, and custom tools are present in the code but not in the advertised tool list.
`max_rows` can cap returned rows for `execute_sql`, but it does not remove SECRET/UNTRUSTED because capped results may still contain sensitive or attacker-authored data.

execute_sql.rationale: `execute_sql` accepts an arbitrary `sql` string and passes it to the configured connector via `connector.executeSQL(sql, executeOptions)`, then returns `result.resultSets` as `statements` including database `rows`. This can expose non-public data from the configured database, so SECRET applies. It is not advertised as read-only here, and absent a `readonly` tool setting the policy permits DML/DDL/admin/unknown SQL, so it can change database state. UNTRUSTED is kept because arbitrary returned database rows may contain attacker-authored content in multi-writer/user-content databases; the code does not establish whether this sqlite source is single-writer trusted, so this is undetermined. No SINK label: the code sends SQL only to the configured database connector, not to an agent-chosen attacker-readable host or public destination. No HOSTEXEC evidence in the provided code.

search_objects.rationale: `search_objects` connects to the configured database and returns schema/object metadata such as schemas, tables, columns, indexes, comments, stored procedure details, and definitions. Database metadata can be non-public, so SECRET applies. UNTRUSTED is kept because names/comments/descriptions/definitions can be authored by other database users in a multi-writer database; the code does not settle whether this source is trusted-only, so this is undetermined. The tool is read-only in code: it searches metadata and its row-count fallback executes a `SELECT COUNT(*)` with `{ readonly: true }`. No SINK: it does not contact an agent-chosen host or write to an attacker-readable destination.

value_conditions.effect: The built-in tools `execute_sql` and `search_objects` are enabled by default for a source when that source has no configured tools.
value_conditions.syntax: default with no TOML [[tools]] entry for a source

value_conditions.effect: When any tools are configured for a source, only those listed are registered for that source; omitting a built-in removes it from the advertised tools for that source.
value_conditions.syntax: TOML [[tools]] entries for a source omitting `name = "execute_sql"` or `name = "search_objects"`

value_conditions.effect: Denies non-read SQL classes for `execute_sql`, removing its ability to change database state, but it can still return database data so SECRET/UNTRUSTED remain.
Uses an in-memory sample SQLite database rather than the user's configured private database, so SECRET does not apply to demo sample data.
